title: The US Needs a Data Strategy for the AI Era, but Should Not Copy China
gist: A USCC report ('The People's Republic of Data') urges Washington to copy China's data-as-asset machinery (balance-sheet data accounting, state data exchanges), but the authors argue China itself is abandoning that model after concluding data cannot be assetized ex ante.

insights.claim: In August 2026 the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission issued 'The People's Republic of Data', arguing China spent a decade building machinery to turn data into capital, including rules letting companies book data as a balance-sheet asset and state-run data exchanges.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
entities: U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission
insights.so_what: Signals congressional attention to a US national data strategy that could shape AI-era data regulation.

insights.claim: The USCC report advises Congress to craft a comprehensive US data strategy and to consider whether US accounting standards should recognize data as an asset.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
entities: U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission
insights.so_what: Any move to let data be capitalized on balance sheets would affect reported assets of data-rich tech/AI companies; low probability but worth tracking.
insights.quote: consider whether U.S. accounting standards should recognize data as an asset

insights.claim: China is already moving beyond the data-as-tradable-asset model that the USCC report urges Washington to study, so copying it would mean adopting a policy Beijing is abandoning.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Be skeptical of US policy proposals modeled on China's data exchanges; the lead indicator is Beijing's own policy shift.
insights.quote: China itself is already moving beyond the model it is urging Washington to study.
insights.locator: The report is right to note

insights.claim: After years of treating data as a strategic commodity to be owned and traded, Chinese policymakers have concluded that data cannot be assetized ex ante, i.e. its value cannot be fixed before use.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Undercuts the investment case for data-exchange and data-asset-accounting plays in China; value accrues to data use (e.g. AI applications) rather than data ownership.
insights.quote: Data cannot be assetized ex ante.

top_entities: U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission
